message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the most recent common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** (to which lions belong) and **Perissodactyla** (to which zebras belong).  

Both orders are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, so the common ancestor would have been a small, insectivorous or omnivorous mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous to early Paleogene. This ancestor would have possessed the basic mammalian body plan and the early features that later gave rise to the diverse lineages of carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Both are mammals, but lions are felids (family Felidae), zebras are equids (family Equidae). They diverged from a common ancestor in the order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla? Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps a placental mammal ancestor. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the eutherian ancestor. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the superorders Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That would be a mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is a mammal from the Laurasiatheria clade, likely a small, insectivorous mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. Or we can say: the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla, which is a member of the Laurasiatheria clade. So the answer: a small, insectivorous mammal from the late Cretaceous/Eocene. Or we can mention the genus "Eutheria" or "Laurasiatheria". The question might be answered simply: "The last common ancestor of lion and zebra is a mammal from the Laurasiatheria clade that lived about 70-80 million years ago." Or "the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is a small, insectivorous mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago." So answer accordingly. No tool needed.
